summary.text: Krakatoa, a volcanic island in the Sunda Strait in today's Indonesia, erupted for more than five months in 1883, with its biggest eruption on 27 August.
That day's eruption destroyed over 70% of the island and the islands around it, and the island collapsed into a caldera.
Its third explosion that day is the loudest sound known in history, heard 4,800 km away, and at least 36,417 deaths are blamed on the eruption and its tsunamis.

items.prompt: Krakatoa sat in a sea strait between Java and Sumatra. Besides the eruption itself, what caused deaths on the coasts nearby?

options.label: Lava rivers flowing across the sea
Tsunamis set off by the eruption
A hurricane formed by the ash cloud
Poisoned wells from falling pumice

items.explain: The explosions triggered tsunamis that struck Java and Sumatra, and the deaths are attributed to the eruption and those tsunamis.

items.prompt: How far from Krakatoa was its loudest explosion heard?

options.label: About 50 kilometres
About 300 kilometres
About 4,800 kilometres
Only on the island itself

items.explain: The blast was heard in Perth, 3,110 km away, and on Rodrigues near Mauritius, 4,800 km away.

items.prompt: After the eruption of 27 August 1883, what became of most of Krakatoa island?

options.label: It grew into a much taller cone
It split into two equal islands
It was buried under a lava dome
It collapsed into a caldera

items.explain: The eruption destroyed over 70% of the island and its nearby islands, and the island collapsed into a caldera.

items.prompt: In early August 1883 an engineer landed on Krakatoa and found ash half a metre deep and only tree stumps left. What did he advise?

options.label: Against making any further landings
Building a lookout post on the summit
Replanting the forest straight away
Moving nearby villagers onto the island

items.explain: Captain Ferzenaar saw a thick ash layer and all vegetation destroyed, and advised against any further landings.

items.prompt: Krakatoa's third explosion on 27 August holds what record?

options.label: The tallest ash column ever seen
The loudest sound ever measured
The largest volume ever erupted
The longest eruption ever recorded

items.explain: The third explosion, at 10:02 a.m., was the loudest sound that has ever been measured.

items.prompt: On Rodrigues, an island 4,800 km away, people heard Krakatoa's biggest blast. What did they take the noise to be?

options.label: Waves crashing against a sea cliff
A rockslide in the island's hills
Cannon fire from a nearby ship
Thunder from a passing storm

items.explain: People on Rodrigues took the distant sound of the blast for cannon fire from a ship nearby.
